There were a few positives for Sri Lanka, namely the way their pacers bowled with the 
new ball. Kumara, though, limped off in the dying embers and Sri Lanka would be hoping 
that that is nothing serious. With the T20I series on the horizon, there is something for 
Sri Lanka to cling on to, although they would need a drastic improvement in the batting 
department to pose a stiff challenge. 
Earlier in the day, New Zealand's bowlers were brilliant, with Henry, Shipley and Mitchell 
picking up three-wicket hauls. Sri Lanka, much like the rest of the tour so far, were not 
able to withstand that pressure and crumbled to a score that was well below par. 
But like he has done in his short ODI career so far, Young stood up, soaked in the 
pressure and stitched together an excellent knock. Nicholls provided him good support, 
with the pair ultimately putting on a century stand.
